_readme: Reference specification and expected output for labour and plant rates.
Shown at the foot of the labour edit popup so an estimator can sanity-check a
day rate against what the item actually produces in a day.
Every 'output' is a RANGE with the assumption it rests on, never a single
figure. Published sources disagree by a factor of two for the same machine —
one gives 27 m3/hr for a 75 hp dozer in clay and 43.5 in sand and gravel —
because output is governed by soil, haul distance, operator and site far more
than by the machine. A single authoritative-looking number in an estimating
tool would be read as a promise, so the basis travels with the figure.
Keyed by LabourName. Lookups go through RateNameAliases, so an entry keeps
working after the catalogue is renamed.
Fields: spec, output, basis, running, source. Any may be omitted.
An item with no entry simply shows nothing — absence is not an error.

Bulldozer D4.spec: Cat D4-class crawler dozer. ~130 hp, ~9 t operating weight, straight or semi-U blade.
Bulldozer D4.basis: 15-30 m haul, common earth, competent operator. Clay drops it by roughly a third; sand and gravel lifts it.
Bulldozer D4.source: Caterpillar published specifications; earthmoving productivity tables (planningengineer.net)

Bulldozer D6.spec: Cat D6-class crawler dozer. Up to 345 hp (C9.3 ACERT), ~23 t operating weight, blade capacity to ~7.3 t.
Bulldozer D6.basis: 30 m haul, common earth. Longer hauls fall away sharply — beyond ~60 m a scraper or truck haul is usually cheaper.
Bulldozer D6.source: Caterpillar / Hawthorne Cat D6 technical specifications; earthmoving productivity tables

Bulldozer D8.spec: Cat D8-class crawler dozer. ~350-450 hp, ~38-40 t operating weight, U or semi-U blade.
Bulldozer D8.basis: 30 m haul, common earth. The usual choice for mass excavation and heavy ripping.
Bulldozer D8.source: Caterpillar published specifications; earthmoving productivity tables

Vibratory wheeled roller (8 to 10 tonnes.spec: Single or double drum vibratory roller, 8-10 t operating weight.
Vibratory wheeled roller (8 to 10 tonnes.output: 80-95 m3/hr compacted, or roughly 600-750 m2/hr of layer
Vibratory wheeled roller (8 to 10 tonnes.basis: 150-200 mm loose layer, 4-6 passes, granular fill at optimum moisture. Cohesive soils need more passes.
Vibratory wheeled roller (8 to 10 tonnes.source: Standard productivity of construction machinery tables (vibratory roller ~91 m3/hr, ~731 m3/day)

Vibratory wheeled roller (10 to 20 tonne.spec: Heavy single drum vibratory roller, 10-20 t operating weight.
Vibratory wheeled roller (10 to 20 tonne.basis: 200-250 mm loose layer, 4-6 passes, granular fill. Suits subgrade and sub-base on road and large platform work.
Vibratory wheeled roller (10 to 20 tonne.source: Standard productivity of construction machinery tables

Pneumatic tyred roller (2.7 to 10 tonnes.spec: Multi-wheel pneumatic tyred roller, 2.7-10 t, ballastable.
Pneumatic tyred roller (2.7 to 10 tonnes.basis: Kneading action — used for sealing and finishing asphalt and for cohesive fills where a vibrating drum is unsuitable.
Pneumatic tyred roller (2.7 to 10 tonnes.source: Standard productivity of construction machinery tables

Pneumatic tyred roller (10 to 20 tonnes).spec: Multi-wheel pneumatic tyred roller, 10-20 t, ballastable.
Pneumatic tyred roller (10 to 20 tonnes).basis: Intermediate rolling on asphalt, or proof rolling of formation.
Pneumatic tyred roller (10 to 20 tonnes).source: Standard productivity of construction machinery tables

Pneumatic tyred roller (20 to 31.8 tonne.spec: Heavy ballasted pneumatic tyred roller, 20-31.8 t.
Pneumatic tyred roller (20 to 31.8 tonne.basis: Heavy proof rolling and deep lift compaction on highway work.
Pneumatic tyred roller (20 to 31.8 tonne.source: Standard productivity of construction machinery tables

Static steel wheeled roller - (2.7 to 6.spec: Tandem or three-wheel static steel roller, 2.7-6 t, no vibration.
Static steel wheeled roller - (2.7 to 6.basis: Finishing passes and thin layers. Static rolling is for surface regularity, not deep compaction.
Static steel wheeled roller - (2.7 to 6.source: Standard productivity of construction machinery tables

Static steel wheeled roller - (6 to 12.7.basis: Breakdown and finish rolling on asphalt; final passes on granular formation.
Static steel wheeled roller - (6 to 12.7.source: Standard productivity of construction machinery tables

Generator - 1.5/5 KVA.spec: Small portable petrol or diesel set, 1.5-5 kVA (~1.2-4 kW usable).
Generator - 1.5/5 KVA.output: Runs hand tools, site lighting, a small vibrator poker
Generator - 1.5/5 KVA.basis: kW is about 0.8 x kVA at unity-ish site loads. Size to about 75% load for fuel economy and engine life.
Generator - 1.5/5 KVA.source: Diesel generator fuel consumption charts (John F Hunt, FW Power)

Generator - 10/15 KVA.spec: Small site set, 10-15 kVA (~8-12 kW usable).
Generator - 10/15 KVA.basis: At 15 kVA: about 1.8 l/hr at half load, 3.2 l/hr at full.
Generator - 10/15 KVA.source: Diesel generator fuel consumption charts (John F Hunt, FW Power)

Generator - 27/35 KVA.output: Mixed site load: mixer, vibrators, lighting, welding at low duty
Generator - 27/35 KVA.basis: Roughly a quarter of rated kVA in litres per hour at full load.

Generator - 50/80 KVA.output: Whole small site, or a tower crane on light duty
Generator - 50/80 KVA.basis: Fuel is close to linear with load, not with rating — a lightly loaded set still burns a third of full-load fuel.

Generator - 125 KVA.output: Main site supply for a medium project
Generator - 125 KVA.basis: A 100 kVA class set burns about 11 l/hr at half load and about 21 l/hr at full.
Generator - 125 KVA.source: Diesel generator fuel consumption charts (asogenset, Econo Solar)

Generator - 150 KVA.output: Main site supply, batching plant, multiple tower cranes
Generator - 150 KVA.basis: Sized on starting current as much as running load — motors draw several times running current on start.

Generator - 200 KVA.output: Main supply for a large site
Generator - 200 KVA.basis: Fuel dominates the hire cost at this size — at Nigerian diesel prices a full-load day can exceed the day rate itself.

Generator - 250 KVA.output: Main supply for a large site or batching plant
Generator - 250 KVA.basis: At 250 kVA: about 25 l/hr at half load and about 50 l/hr at full.
Generator - 250 KVA.source: Diesel generator fuel consumption charts (John F Hunt)

Concrete mixer 10/7.spec: Tilting drum mixer. 10 cu ft drum, 7 cu ft batch — about 0.20 m3 of mixed concrete per batch.
Concrete mixer 10/7.basis: About 12-15 batches an hour on a 4-5 minute cycle including charge and discharge. Batch capacity is 60-80% of drum volume because the drum mixes at an angle.
Concrete mixer 10/7.source: Concrete mixer capacity guides (AMIX Systems, EZG Manufacturing)

Concrete mixer 14/10.spec: Tilting drum mixer. 14 cu ft drum, 10 cu ft batch — about 0.28 m3 per batch.
Concrete mixer 14/10.basis: 12-15 batches an hour. The usual one-mixer site pour size.

Concrete mixer 21/14.spec: Tilting drum mixer. 21 cu ft drum, 14 cu ft batch — about 0.40 m3 per batch.
Concrete mixer 21/14.basis: 12-15 batches an hour. Beyond roughly 30 m3 in a pour, ready-mix usually wins on cost and on cold-joint risk.

Mason.spec: Skilled bricklayer or blocklayer, normally working with one helper.
Mason.basis: 8-hour day with 1 helper, walling to 3 m height. Plastering by the same trade: about 12 m2/day internal, 8 m2/day external.
Mason.source: Standard labour output tables (out-turn work schedules)

Carpenter.spec: Skilled formwork and joinery carpenter, normally with one helper.
Carpenter.output: 5.5-6.5 m2/day general; about 14 m2/day slab shuttering
Carpenter.basis: 8-hour day with 1 helper. Slab soffits run faster than columns and beams, which are cut-heavy.

Steelfixer.spec: Reinforcement cutter, bender and fixer, normally with one helper.
Steelfixer.basis: 8-hour day with 1 helper. Where steel arrives cut and bent, placing alone runs far higher: about 320 kg/day in slabs, 380 in columns and beams, 450-520 in foundations and rafts.

Tiler.spec: Floor and wall tiler, normally with one helper.
Tiler.output: 12 m2/day vitrified floor, 10 m2/day ceramic floor, 8 m2/day ceramic wall
Tiler.basis: 8-hour day with 1 helper. Wall tiling is slower than floor; small formats and cut-heavy rooms slower again.

Foreman.spec: Trade foreman. Runs the working face: sets out, allocates gangs, checks quality and keeps the programme.
Foreman.output: No direct output — governs everyone else's
Foreman.basis: Normally one per 20-40 operatives. Under-manning supervision is a common cause of the output figures elsewhere in this library not being met.
Foreman.running: Supervisory; costed as a fixed head on the gang, not per unit
Foreman.source: Standard labour output tables (out-turn work schedules); MEP production rate tables

Headman.spec: Charge hand or ganger. Working supervisor over an unskilled gang.
Headman.output: Works at about half a labourer's output while supervising
Headman.source: Standard labour output tables (out-turn work schedules); MEP production rate tables

MEP foreman.spec: Mechanical, electrical and plumbing foreman. Coordinates services against the builder's work.
MEP foreman.output: No direct output — governs the MEP gangs
MEP foreman.basis: Normally one per 15-30 MEP operatives. Services work is sequencing-heavy, so supervision carries more weight here than on civils.
MEP foreman.running: Supervisory; fixed head on the gang
MEP foreman.source: Standard labour output tables (out-turn work schedules); MEP production rate tables

Labourer.spec: General unskilled operative. Handles materials, mixes, barrows, cleans and assists trades.
Labourer.output: 4-6 m3/day moved by barrow, or supports one tradesman continuously
Labourer.basis: 8-hour day, 20-30 m barrow run. Output falls away sharply beyond about 40 m — past that a dumper is cheaper than more labourers.
Labourer.running: Usually costed in a gang rather than alone
Labourer.source: Standard labour output tables (out-turn work schedules); MEP production rate tables

Semi skilled.spec: Operative working under direction on repetitive tasks: simple formwork, block handling, backfill.
Semi skilled.output: About 60-75% of a tradesman's output on the same task
Semi skilled.basis: 8-hour day under a skilled tradesman or charge hand.
Semi skilled.running: Gang: paired with a skilled trade
Semi skilled.source: Standard labour output tables (out-turn work schedules); MEP production rate tables

Skilled/Artisan.spec: General skilled tradesman where the trade is not separately listed.
Skilled/Artisan.output: Priced against the specific trade — see the named trades for figures
Skilled/Artisan.basis: 8-hour day. Use this only where the work does not fall to a named trade; a named trade carries a firmer output.
Skilled/Artisan.source: Standard labour output tables (out-turn work schedules); MEP production rate tables

Glazier.spec: Glass and glazing fixer, working with one helper.
Glazier.basis: 8-hour day with 1 helper, panes to about 2 m2 at low level. Large panes and anything needing a lift or scaffold run well below this.
Glazier.source: Standard labour output tables (out-turn work schedules); MEP production rate tables

Welder.spec: Site welder, arc or MIG, working to structural or pipework standards.
Welder.output: 25-40 m/day single-pass fillet; 8-15 m/day multi-pass structural butt
Welder.basis: 8-hour day at ground level. Overhead, positional and site-tested welds fall to the bottom of the range or below. Add for grinding, preparation and NDT standing time.
Welder.running: Gang: 1 welder + 1 helper; consumables and machine costed separately
Welder.source: Standard labour output tables (out-turn work schedules); MEP production rate tables

Electrician (skilled).spec: Installation electrician: conduit, wiring, accessories and terminations.
Electrician (skilled).basis: 8-hour day, first or final fix, normal domestic and commercial heights. Wiring pulled into installed conduit runs far faster, about 200 m/day.
Electrician (skilled).source: Standard labour output tables (out-turn work schedules); MEP production rate tables

Electrician mate.spec: Assists the electrician: chases, pulls, fetches, holds and cleans.
Electrician mate.output: No separate output — the gang rate assumes one mate per electrician
Electrician mate.basis: 8-hour day. The electrician figures in this library already include a mate; do not count the output twice.
Electrician mate.source: Standard labour output tables (out-turn work schedules); MEP production rate tables

Wireman / cable puller.spec: Pulls and dresses cable into installed containment.
Wireman / cable puller.basis: 8-hour day into conduit or tray already in place, straight runs. Heavy multicore, long draws and tight bends cut this substantially.
Wireman / cable puller.running: Gang: normally 2 working together on a draw
Wireman / cable puller.source: Standard labour output tables (out-turn work schedules); MEP production rate tables

Plumber (skilled).spec: Installation plumber: water supply, waste and sanitary fittings.
Plumber (skilled).output: 8-10 m/day supply pipe, 6-8 m/day drain pipe, or about 3 toilets/day
Plumber (skilled).basis: 8-hour day with helpers. Buried 150 mm uPVC drainage to 1 m deep, including dig, bed, lay and backfill, runs 30-35 m/day as a complete operation.
Plumber (skilled).source: Standard labour output tables (out-turn work schedules); MEP production rate tables

Plumber mate.spec: Assists the plumber: carries, cuts, holds, chases and tests.
Plumber mate.output: No separate output — the plumber's gang rate assumes a mate
Plumber mate.basis: 8-hour day. Counted in the plumber figures already; do not add it twice.
Plumber mate.source: Standard labour output tables (out-turn work schedules); MEP production rate tables

Pipefitter (PPR fusion and uPVC solvent.spec: Fitter working in PPR by heat fusion and uPVC by solvent weld.
Pipefitter (PPR fusion and uPVC solvent.output: 30-60 joints/day, or 20-30 m/day of run pipe
Pipefitter (PPR fusion and uPVC solvent.basis: 8-hour day, 20-63 mm pipe at accessible heights. Fusion needs the joint held to cool; solvent needs cure time before pressure — both cap how fast a run can close.
Pipefitter (PPR fusion and uPVC solvent.source: Standard labour output tables (out-turn work schedules); MEP production rate tables

Heavy plant operator.spec: Operates tracked and heavy wheeled plant: dozers, excavators, graders, large loaders.
Heavy plant operator.output: No output of its own — the machine's output is the operator's
Heavy plant operator.basis: 8-hour day. Operator skill is one of the largest single variables in every plant figure in this library; the published ranges assume a competent, regular operator.
Heavy plant operator.running: One per machine, plus a banksman on blind or trafficked areas
Heavy plant operator.source: Standard labour output tables (out-turn work schedules); MEP production rate tables

Light plant operator.spec: Operates small plant: mixers, pumps, compactors, small loaders, hoists.
Light plant operator.output: No output of its own — the machine's output is the operator's
Light plant operator.basis: 8-hour day. One operator commonly runs several small items on a small site.
Light plant operator.running: One per machine or group of small machines
Light plant operator.source: Standard labour output tables (out-turn work schedules); MEP production rate tables

Heavy vehicle driver.spec: Drives tipper lorries, low-loaders and heavy haulage.
Heavy vehicle driver.output: No output of its own — the vehicle's cycle is the output
Heavy vehicle driver.basis: 8-hour day. Haulage output is set by cycle time, not by the driver: load, haul, tip, return.
Heavy vehicle driver.source: Standard labour output tables (out-turn work schedules); MEP production rate tables

Light vehicle driver.spec: Drives pick-ups, vans and small tippers for site logistics.
Light vehicle driver.output: No output of its own — the vehicle's cycle is the output
Light vehicle driver.source: Standard labour output tables (out-turn work schedules); MEP production rate tables

Excavator-JCB 3C or similar model.spec: Backhoe loader, JCB 3CX class. About 100 hp, 1.0 m3 front loader bucket, roughly 0.3 m3 rear backhoe bucket, digging depth to about 5.9 m.
Excavator-JCB 3C or similar model.output: 20-40 m3/hr excavating; higher on loading duties
Excavator-JCB 3C or similar model.basis: Trench and general excavation in common earth, spoil alongside. The most versatile machine on a small site, but slower than a tracked excavator of the same weight on sustained bulk dig.
Excavator-JCB 3C or similar model.source: JCB 3CX published specifications; earthmoving productivity tables

Excavator 635.spec: Tracked hydraulic excavator, smaller class — around 0.6-0.8 m3 bucket, roughly 15-20 t.
Excavator 635.basis: Bulk dig in common earth, loading to lorry alongside. NOTE: 635 is a local size code, not a manufacturer model — confirm the bucket size of the machine actually hired, as output moves with it almost proportionally.
Excavator 635.source: Standard productivity of construction machinery tables; manufacturer published specifications

Excavator 935.spec: Tracked hydraulic excavator, larger class — around 1.0-1.4 m3 bucket, roughly 20-30 t.
Excavator 935.basis: Bulk dig in common earth, loading alongside. NOTE: 935 is a local size code, not a manufacturer model — confirm the bucket size of the machine hired.
Excavator 935.source: Standard productivity of construction machinery tables; manufacturer published specifications

Payloader 635.spec: Wheeled or crawler loader, smaller class — around 0.8-1.0 m3 bucket.
Payloader 635.basis: Stockpile loading to lorry, short travel. Based on a 0.45-0.55 minute basic cycle at about 75% job efficiency. NOTE: 635 is a local size code, not a manufacturer model.
Payloader 635.source: Caterpillar wheel loader productivity method; standard productivity tables

Payloader 935.spec: Loader, Cat 935 class — about 1.0 m3 heaped bucket, roughly 8.8 t operating weight.
Payloader 935.basis: Stockpile loading with short travel, 0.45-0.55 minute cycle at about 75% efficiency. Output falls quickly once travel exceeds about 30 m — past that, load to a lorry instead of carrying.
Payloader 935.source: Caterpillar 935C published specifications; Cat wheel loader productivity method

Grader (Cat 140G).spec: Cat 140G motor grader. 150 hp Cat 3306, 12 ft (3.7 m) moldboard, about 12.6 t, built 1987-95 and common secondhand in West Africa.
Grader (Cat 140G).basis: Fine trimming to level on sub-base. Spreading and heavy cutting are slower; a light finishing pass is faster. Several passes are normal, so divide by the number of passes for net progress.
Grader (Cat 140G).source: Caterpillar 140G published specifications; standard productivity tables

Plate compactor.spec: Walk-behind vibrating plate, petrol or diesel, typically 60-90 kg.
Plate compactor.basis: 100-150 mm loose layer, 3-4 passes, granular fill. For trench and edge work where a roller cannot reach. Not a substitute for a roller on layers over about 150 mm.
Plate compactor.source: Standard productivity of construction machinery tables; manufacturer published specifications

Dumper.spec: Site dumper, forward tipping, typically 1-9 t payload.
Dumper.basis: 100-200 m round trip on site roads. Displaces about 4-6 barrow labourers over that distance; the crossover is around 40 m.
Dumper.source: Standard productivity of construction machinery tables; manufacturer published specifications

Tipping lorry-10 ton.spec: Rigid tipper, about 10 t payload — roughly 6-7 m3 of loose earth.
Tipping lorry-10 ton.output: 3-5 loads/day at 20 km; 8-12 loads/day at 5 km
Tipping lorry-10 ton.basis: Round trip including load, haul, tip and return. Haul distance governs everything: match the number of lorries to the loader so neither waits.
Tipping lorry-10 ton.source: Standard productivity of construction machinery tables; manufacturer published specifications

Tipping lorry-20 ton.spec: Rigid tipper, about 20 t payload — roughly 12-14 m3 of loose earth.
Tipping lorry-20 ton.output: 3-5 loads/day at 20 km; 7-10 loads/day at 5 km
Tipping lorry-20 ton.basis: Round trip including load, haul, tip and return. Fewer, larger loads cut cycle count but need a loader big enough not to become the bottleneck.
Tipping lorry-20 ton.source: Standard productivity of construction machinery tables; manufacturer published specifications

Tipping lorry-30 ton.spec: Rigid or articulated tipper, about 30 t payload — roughly 18-20 m3 of loose earth.
Tipping lorry-30 ton.output: 3-4 loads/day at 20 km; 6-9 loads/day at 5 km
Tipping lorry-30 ton.basis: Round trip. Worth it only on long hauls and good roads; on short site hauls the loading wait cancels the payload gain.
Tipping lorry-30 ton.source: Standard productivity of construction machinery tables; manufacturer published specifications

Barge (100 ton capacity).spec: Flat-top marine barge, 100 t payload, normally towed or pushed.
Barge (100 ton capacity).output: 1-3 round trips/day depending on the crossing
Barge (100 ton capacity).basis: Governed by tide, loading facilities and tow speed rather than by the barge. Used where a road haul is impossible or far longer.
Barge (100 ton capacity).running: Tug fuel and crew costed separately
Barge (100 ton capacity).source: Standard productivity of construction machinery tables; manufacturer published specifications

Crane-80 ton - crawler track type..spec: Crawler-mounted lattice or telescopic crane, 80 t maximum rated capacity.
Crane-80 ton - crawler track type..basis: Rated capacity is at minimum radius. Safe load falls steeply with radius — at working radius an 80 t crane may lift only 10-20 t, which is the figure that matters when planning.
Crane-80 ton - crawler track type..running: Diesel ~20-30 l/hr; plus assembly and dismantling time
Crane-80 ton - crawler track type..source: Standard productivity of construction machinery tables; manufacturer published specifications

Crane-120 ton - crawler track type..spec: Crawler-mounted lattice crane, 120 t maximum rated capacity.
Crane-120 ton - crawler track type..basis: Rated at minimum radius; derate heavily for working radius. Allow separate days for erection and dismantling — often several.
Crane-120 ton - crawler track type..running: Diesel ~25-40 l/hr; plus assembly and dismantling
Crane-120 ton - crawler track type..source: Standard productivity of construction machinery tables; manufacturer published specifications

Crane-150 ton - crawler track type..spec: Crawler-mounted lattice crane, 150 t maximum rated capacity.
Crane-150 ton - crawler track type..basis: Rated at minimum radius. At this size, ground bearing pressure and crane mats usually need designing, and that cost belongs in the rate.
Crane-150 ton - crawler track type..running: Diesel ~30-45 l/hr; plus assembly and dismantling
Crane-150 ton - crawler track type..source: Standard productivity of construction machinery tables; manufacturer published specifications

Mobile crane-30 ton.spec: Truck or all-terrain mobile crane, 30 t maximum rated capacity.
Mobile crane-30 ton.basis: Rated at minimum radius. Sets up in under an hour on firm level ground, which is why it beats a crawler for short duration work.
Mobile crane-30 ton.source: Standard productivity of construction machinery tables; manufacturer published specifications

Mobile crane-60 ton.spec: All-terrain mobile crane, 60 t maximum rated capacity.
Mobile crane-60 ton.basis: Rated at minimum radius; outrigger loads need checking against slabs and buried services.
Mobile crane-60 ton.source: Standard productivity of construction machinery tables; manufacturer published specifications

Mobile crane-80 ton.spec: All-terrain mobile crane, 80 t maximum rated capacity.
Mobile crane-80 ton.basis: Rated at minimum radius. May need counterweight delivered separately, which is an extra vehicle movement to price.
Mobile crane-80 ton.source: Standard productivity of construction machinery tables; manufacturer published specifications

Paving Machine 4 - 8 ft laying width..spec: Asphalt paver, 1.2-2.4 m variable screed width.
Paving Machine 4 - 8 ft laying width..basis: Continuous supply at a steady speed. At this width it suits car parks, estate roads and patching; highway pavers of 3-4 m reach 200-400 t/hr. Output is set by the lorries feeding it, not the paver.
Paving Machine 4 - 8 ft laying width..source: Standard productivity of construction machinery tables; manufacturer published specifications

Compressor.spec: Towable diesel air compressor, typically 100-250 cfm.
Compressor.basis: Each hammer needs roughly 60-90 cfm. Sizing on the number of tools, not the pressure, is what keeps them all working.
Compressor.source: Standard productivity of construction machinery tables; manufacturer published specifications

Jack - Hammer (Small).spec: Handheld pneumatic or electric breaker, roughly 10-15 kg.
Jack - Hammer (Small).basis: Unreinforced concrete and screed, working from a free edge. Reinforcement roughly halves it. Needs about 60 cfm of air.
Jack - Hammer (Small).source: Standard productivity of construction machinery tables; manufacturer published specifications

Jack - Hammer (Medium).basis: Mass concrete and slabs from a free edge. Reinforcement roughly halves it. About 75 cfm of air.
Jack - Hammer (Medium).source: Standard productivity of construction machinery tables; manufacturer published specifications

Jack - Hammer (Big).spec: Heavy handheld pneumatic breaker, roughly 30-40 kg.
Jack - Hammer (Big).basis: Heavy mass concrete and rock. Two operators normally rotate — the limit is the man, not the tool. About 90 cfm of air.
Jack - Hammer (Big).source: Standard productivity of construction machinery tables; manufacturer published specifications

Concrete cutting machine.spec: Walk-behind or handheld disc saw for concrete and asphalt.
Concrete cutting machine.basis: Straight cuts in unreinforced slab. Depth and reinforcement both cut this sharply; a full-depth cut through a reinforced slab may run under 10 m/hr. Blade wear is a real consumable cost.
Concrete cutting machine.running: Petrol or electric; water feed and blades costed separately
Concrete cutting machine.source: Standard productivity of construction machinery tables; manufacturer published specifications

Cutting machine.spec: Abrasive cut-off saw for steel bar, section and pipe.
Cutting machine.output: 60-120 cuts/hr in bar up to 25 mm
Cutting machine.basis: Bench work, straight square cuts. Large sections and stainless run far slower and eat discs.
Cutting machine.running: Electric; cutting discs are the running cost
Cutting machine.source: Standard productivity of construction machinery tables; manufacturer published specifications

Poker vibrator (electrical).spec: Immersion poker with electric drive, typically 25-60 mm head.
Poker vibrator (electrical).basis: Insert vertically, hold 5-15 seconds until air stops rising, withdraw slowly, repeat at about 500 mm centres. The wide range is real: placing method governs it more than the poker does.
Poker vibrator (electrical).source: Concrete compaction guidance (poker vibrator technique); standard productivity tables

Poker vibrator (mechanical).spec: Immersion poker driven by a petrol or diesel unit, typically 25-60 mm head.
Poker vibrator (mechanical).basis: As the electric poker, but independent of a power supply — the usual choice where no generator is on the pour. Same 500 mm insertion spacing and 5-15 second dwell.
Poker vibrator (mechanical).source: Concrete compaction guidance; standard productivity tables

Concrete pumping machine (Dry - mix).spec: Trailer or static concrete pump fed with a dry or semi-dry mix.
Concrete pumping machine (Dry - mix).basis: Rated output is 30-50 m3/hr; expect 60-80% of rating in practice. Dry mixes block more readily, so line cleaning and downtime belong in the rate.
Concrete pumping machine (Dry - mix).running: Diesel ~10-18 l/hr; plus line, cleaning and standby
Concrete pumping machine (Dry - mix).source: Standard productivity of construction machinery tables; manufacturer published specifications

Concrete pumping machine (Wet - mix).spec: Line or boom concrete pump fed with a pumpable wet mix.
Concrete pumping machine (Wet - mix).basis: Line pumps rate 60-90 m3/hr and boom pumps 60-130; expect 60-80% of rating. Needs a designed pump mix with extra sand and cement — pricing it as ordinary concrete understates the material cost.
Concrete pumping machine (Wet - mix).running: Diesel ~15-25 l/hr; plus line, cleaning and standby
Concrete pumping machine (Wet - mix).source: Standard productivity of construction machinery tables; manufacturer published specifications

Welding machine (small).spec: Portable arc welding set, roughly 140-250 A.
Welding machine (small).output: Supports one welder continuously on light work
Welding machine (small).basis: Duty cycle is the limit: at 60% a set welds six minutes in ten. Light fabrication, handrails, brackets.
Welding machine (small).running: Electric or petrol; electrodes costed separately
Welding machine (small).source: Standard productivity of construction machinery tables; manufacturer published specifications

Welding machine (big).spec: Heavy-duty or engine-driven welding set, roughly 300-600 A.
Welding machine (big).output: Supports one to two welders on structural work
Welding machine (big).basis: Higher duty cycle and heavier electrodes for structural and pipework. Engine-driven sets suit sites with no reliable power.
Welding machine (big).running: Diesel ~3-6 l/hr if engine-driven; electrodes separate
Welding machine (big).source: Standard productivity of construction machinery tables; manufacturer published specifications

Gas torch and 50 or 70mm burner..spec: Oxy-acetylene cutting and heating set with 50 or 70 mm burner nozzle.
Gas torch and 50 or 70mm burner..basis: Straight cuts in mild steel. Thicker plate, bevels and overhead work run slower. Gas is a significant consumable — meter it rather than treating the set as a flat hire.
Gas torch and 50 or 70mm burner..source: Standard productivity of construction machinery tables; manufacturer published specifications

Pipe threading machine; up to 50mm.spec: Powered pipe threading machine for steel pipe to 50 mm.
Pipe threading machine; up to 50mm.basis: 8-hour day, bench mounted, cut and thread. Larger diameters and site work well below this. Dies and cutting oil are consumables.
Pipe threading machine; up to 50mm.source: Standard labour output tables (out-turn work schedules); MEP production rate tables

PPR fusion welding machine; 20 to 63mm.spec: Socket fusion welder for PPR pipe, 20-63 mm.
PPR fusion welding machine; 20 to 63mm.basis: Each joint is heated, joined and held to cool — the cooling hold is what caps the rate, not the machine.
PPR fusion welding machine; 20 to 63mm.source: Standard labour output tables (out-turn work schedules); MEP production rate tables

Cable rod set and draw tape.spec: Glass-fibre rod set and steel or nylon draw tape for pulling cable through conduit.
Cable rod set and draw tape.output: Supports about 200 m/day of cable pulling
Cable rod set and draw tape.basis: Straight runs in installed conduit. Long draws and multiple bends need two operatives and a lubricant.
Cable rod set and draw tape.source: Standard labour output tables (out-turn work schedules); MEP production rate tables

Earth resistance tester (megger).spec: Earth resistance and insulation resistance tester.
Earth resistance tester (megger).basis: Testing and certification, not installation. Instrument needs periodic calibration, and an uncalibrated instrument fails a witnessed test — carry that cost.
Earth resistance tester (megger).running: Battery; calibration is the running cost
Earth resistance tester (megger).source: Standard labour output tables (out-turn work schedules); MEP production rate tables

Sand Pot for sand blasting.spec: Pressure pot abrasive blasting unit, fed from a compressor.
Sand Pot for sand blasting.basis: Steel to a bright commercial finish. Heavy mill scale and pitting run at the bottom of the range. Abrasive consumption is substantial and is usually the largest cost, not the pot hire.
Sand Pot for sand blasting.running: Compressed air plus abrasive; abrasive is the main consumable
Sand Pot for sand blasting.source: Standard productivity of construction machinery tables; manufacturer published specifications

Respiratory gear for sand blasting.spec: Air-fed blasting hood with breathing-air filtration.
Respiratory gear for sand blasting.output: No output — mandatory protection for the blasting operative
Respiratory gear for sand blasting.basis: One set per blasting operative. Silica exposure without it is a serious and irreversible health risk, so it is a required item on any blasting rate rather than an option.
Respiratory gear for sand blasting.running: Filters and air supply are the running cost
Respiratory gear for sand blasting.source: Standard productivity of construction machinery tables; manufacturer published specifications

Spraying machine.spec: Airless or conventional paint spraying unit.
Spraying machine.basis: Large uninterrupted surfaces, one coat. Roughly three to four times brush and roller output, but masking, edging and overspray protection claw much of that back on cut-up work.
Spraying machine.running: Electric or petrol; tips and filters are consumables
Spraying machine.source: Standard labour output tables (out-turn work schedules); MEP production rate tables

Power Brush.spec: Powered wire brush or rotary surface cleaner.
Power Brush.basis: Light rust, laitance and loose material. Where a specification calls for a blast standard, brushing will not achieve it.
Power Brush.source: Standard productivity of construction machinery tables; manufacturer published specifications

Terrazzo Machine.spec: Rotary terrazzo grinding and polishing machine, water fed.
Terrazzo Machine.basis: Multiple passes through progressively finer stones, plus grouting between passes. First cut on green terrazzo is the slowest.
Terrazzo Machine.running: Electric; stones and water are the running cost
Terrazzo Machine.source: Standard labour output tables (out-turn work schedules); MEP production rate tables
